MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L13·N315unmasked layer
This neuron marks segment boundaries in a "sentence-final" way: it fires positively on the terminal punctuation of a sentence/list item (".", ".\n", "!!\n") — especially just before an abrupt topic shift — while being strongly suppressed on the first word that opens the new sentence ("You", "The", "One", or a clause-initial comma).

This is a weak, low-magnitude neuron with no clean semantic trigger: its (small) positive activations land on mid-sentence continuation tokens that open an elaboration or complete a multiword phrase (an em/en-dash before an appositive list, "off" in "sounding off", "look" in "A look at", the suffix "-ing", a leading "+" bullet), while it is strongly suppressed at structural boundaries — sentence-final ".\n", closing parenthesis of a citation, speaker-name/proper-noun word pieces.
